title: multi-gpu: tune NCCL collectives and overlap comm/compute for tensor-parallel runtime
author: Anika Patel
description: Context: Tensor-parallel multi-GPU workloads at scale show two correlated bottlenecks: (1) suboptimal NCCL collective sizing and stream placement which increases allreduce latency on short sequences, and (2) host/GPU scheduling gaps where communication stalls block useful compute (attention/kernels) leading to lower throughput and higher p99 latency. Motivation: Improve steady-state throughput and tail latency for TP-backed generation workloads (seq_len <= 2048, batch sizes common for RL/serving) without changing public APIs. Summary: This PR introduces a multi-part runtime optimization: 1) NCCL tuning: heuristics to select NCCL algorithm and ring ordering depending on tensor size, topology and NIC presence; enable NCCL_ALGO auto-fallback and tune opportunistic chunk sizing to reduce latency on small allreduces. 2) Overlap comm/compute: introduce asynchronous communication streams for TP collectives and explicit CUDA event synchronization so KV cache/key-value sharding and attention kernels can proceed while cross-GPU collectives are in flight. 3) Fused collectives & pipeline: add a lightweight rung that batches small per-layer allreduces into a fused payload when beneficial (configurable threshold) to reduce per-call overhead. 4) Scheduler changes: runtime scheduler now prioritizes compute worklets that are not stalled on NCCL operations and opportunistically pre-posts recv buffers for upcoming layers. 5) KV cache placement: shard and pin KV cache buffers to per-GPU pinned memory to reduce PCIe stalls and allow overlap with inbound NCCL comms. 6) Telemetry & knobs: expose new metrics (nccl_algo, fused_collective_bytes, comm_compute_overlap_ms) and two new dynamic knobs: TP_FUSE_THRESHOLD_BYTES and TP_COMM_PREPOST_WINDOW_MS. Implementation notes: - C++ runtime changes in runtime/tpu/tensor_parallel/collective_manager.cc and runtime/tpu/tensor_parallel/nccl_utils.cc - CUDA kernels updated to add non-blocking launches and event-based sync in runtime/cuda/kernels/attention.cu - Scheduler updates in runtime/scheduler/scheduler.cc - New unit/integration tests in tests/tp and perf harness updates in benchmarks/perf/tp_nccl_overlap.yaml - Config and documentation updates in docs/perf/tp-nccl-overlap.md Checklist: - [x] NCCL algorithm heuristics implemented - [x] Async streams + event sync implemented - [x] Fused collective logic + config knob - [x] Scheduler prioritization + pre-post logic - [x] Benchmarks and CI tests added - [x] Telemetry events + dashboards stubbed for rollout Backwards compatibility: All changes are runtime-internal and behind a runtime-config flag (TP_COMM_OVERLAP_ENABLED=false by default for safe rollout). No API or on-disk format changes. Related: ENG-3421 (perf spike investigation), ENG-3478 (TP rollout), incident INT-901 (hotfix prototyping).
commits_summary: 4 commits: initial nccl heuristics and utils; async stream + event wiring; fused collective batching and scheduler changes; tests/bench updates and docs
review_conversation: Liam O'Connor (reviewer): Nice work. Can you comment on expected memory overhead for fused collectives? Also need a safety guard when NCCL returns unrecoverable errors.

Author (Anika Patel): Fused collectives only allocate a temporary buffer up to TP_FUSE_THRESHOLD_BYTES (default 16MB). I added retry + fallback to per-call allreduce if NCCL returns NCCL_PROTO_ERROR or other transient failures; persistent failures will surface to runtime error and fall back to single-GPU path where applicable.

Ravi Singh (reviewer): Scheduler changes look good but please add a stress test for many small layers to validate pre-post window sizing. Also, include comment on stream ordering for mixed CPU/GPU RPCs.

Author (Anika Patel): Added tests/tp/test_nccl_overlap.cpp which exercises tiny layers and end-to-end correctness. Added comments around stream ordering and pre-post semantics; the pre-post window is configurable via TP_COMM_PREPOST_WINDOW_MS which defaults to 2ms.
Marta Alvarez (approver): Verified perf dashboard numbers on internal staging cluster (8x A100 80GB) and approve. Ensure metrics names are stable for dashboards.
Liam O'Connor: Approving and merging after CI green.
benchmarks_summary: Internal perf runs on 8x A100 80GB with gpt-medium-like model, batch sizes 1/4/8, seq_len 512/1024: - throughput +18% (avg across configs) - p50 latency -6% - p99 latency -22% especially for small allreduce cases. Fused collectives reduced per-layer allreduce calls by ~65% on models with many small layers. Memory overhead measured < 2% for default thresholds.
release_notes: Performance: Improve multi-GPU tensor-parallel runtime by tuning NCCL collectives, adding comm/compute overlap, and fused collectives. Gives up to ~20% throughput improvement and improved p99 latency for TP-backed generation workloads. Exposed runtime knobs for safe rollout.
testing_notes: Added unit + integration tests under tests/tp; perf harness updated. Ran full CI and internal staging perf on 8x A100 cluster. Stress tests for many small layers included.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: NCCL algorithm changes and async comm increase complexity and could surface hard-to-debug hangs on exotic topologies. Mitigation: feature is behind TP_COMM_OVERLAP_ENABLED flag, added aggressive timeouts and fallback to safe single-call allreduces, added telemetry to detect stuck collectives and automatic disable after repeated failures.
notes_for_release_manager: Gate rollout: enable TP_COMM_OVERLAP_ENABLED only on non-production clusters for 2 weeks. Monitor comm_compute_overlap_ms and nccl_error_rate metrics. Default config keeps feature off.
authors_pr_policy: Engineering: concise description, linked linear tickets, benchmarks included
examples_or_snippets: Code sketch (simplified): cudaStream_t comm_stream; ncclCommInitRank(..., &comm); // pre-post buffers on comm_stream cudaEventRecord(ev_start, comm_stream); launch_attention_kernel(compute_stream); ncclAllReduce(..., comm, comm_stream); cudaEventRecord(ev_end, comm_stream); cudaStreamWaitEvent(compute_stream, ev_end, 0); // continue compute
